questions.q: Why does a pipeline standard written only as a wiki or policy document tend to fail as an organization grows?
options: Wiki pages cannot contain YAML code examples
GitHub automatically deletes documents older than a year
Teams hired after the document was written have never seen it and have no reason to go looking for it
Policy documents are automatically blocked by branch protection rules
questions.explain: A document works for the teams who read it when it was written, but it has no way of reaching a team hired long afterward — the requirement needs to live somewhere every team touches automatically.

questions.q: What does wiring a required job's name into branch protection's required status checks accomplish?
options: The platform refuses to merge a PR until that specific job reports success, regardless of whether anyone remembered the policy
It automatically fixes any failing security scan it finds
It deletes the pull request if the job fails
It removes the need for the shared template entirely
questions.explain: Required status checks make the enforcement structural: merging is blocked at the platform level until the named job reports success, independent of team memory.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend giving teams a narrow, visible override path instead of zero exceptions?
options: Overrides are required by GitHub's terms of service
A standard with zero exceptions tends to get quietly routed around instead of followed
Visible overrides automatically satisfy every required status check
It removes the need for a changelog on the template repo
questions.explain: A rule with no escape hatch for genuine edge cases invites teams to work around it entirely; a visible, logged override keeps the exception on record instead.

questions.q: In the skip-scan-reason example in this lesson, what happens when a team uses the override?
options: The scan still runs silently in the background regardless
The pull request is blocked no matter what reason is given
The override is invisible in the workflow run logs
The skip is recorded as a warning along with the reason, visible in the run and in dashboards
questions.explain: The override input is logged as a warning with the given reason, so the exception is visible rather than silent.

questions.q: What is the 'opposite failure mode' the lesson warns about alongside under-enforcement?
options: Templates having too many optional inputs
Teams forking the shared template without permission
Routing every team's routine pipeline change through one central review queue, turning the platform team into a bottleneck
Pinning consumers to an exact version tag instead of a moving one
questions.explain: Centralizing every change behind one review queue protects consistency but creates a different problem: hundreds of teams waiting on a single bottleneck for changes an automated standard should already cover.
